doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

chapter: Teaching, tradition and the banjo's roots
title: Eras Fleck would visit in a time machine
summary: Fleck would see Bill Monroe and Flatt & Scruggs, early Louis Armstrong and the music of Africans who brought the banjo to America.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Is there is a time in musical history that you wish you could go back to in a time machine?
Just to be hanging out and witness some of that?

Yeah. A lot of the jazz eras, but also a lot of the bluegrass eras. It would have been great to see Bill Monroe, and Flatt & Scruggs playing together in their original bluegrass band. And also a lot of the earlier music before that, the early Louis Armstrong music is well known but a lot of other music that was happening around that time and then the slaves music, the music that was being played on banjos that the Africans that were brought over were playing. A big part of what I’m doing next year, I’m going to Africa for 4 to 6 weeks, to record an album and do some documentary stuff about where the banjo came from.
